land.text: Brittany, Norse-occupied from 919 and reconquered by Alan II; the duchy page's infobox lists 'Brittany' and 'Viking Brittany' as predecessors

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Kingdom of Brittany row ends in 921 and its Duchy of Brittany row begins in 947; the Kingdom of Brittany dossier ends the kingdom in 939.

land.text: the duchy united with France: 'The Estates proclaimed union in 1532'; the infobox gives 'Union with France: 13 August 1547'

successors.note: Cliopatria stops the duchy at 1491 (Anne's marriage to Charles VIII); the pages keep it a distinct duchy, held by the queen-consort, until the 1532 union.

capitals.name: Rennes
capitals.note: The infobox lists Nantes, Rennes and Vannes without years. Rennes is used throughout because the pages show ducal enthronements there (Conan IV 'enthroned at Rennes in 1156'; Anne 'crowned Duchess of Brittany in Rennes on 10 February 1489'); Nantes (Arthur's birthplace) and Vannes were also ducal seats. Unverified as a year-by-year sequence.

correction.text: Brittany under Alan II Barbetorte: the Rennes-Vannes-Cornouaille land of the 947 shape plus the county of Nantes he recovered in 937 (listed as Count of Nantes 938-952)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's first Duchy row begins in 947 but the page dates the duchy from Alan II's victory of 1 August 939 ('Independent duchy (939-942)'). The core is the 947 shape plus Nantes, which the County of Nantes page gives to Alan II as count from 938.

correction.text: The 947 shape plus the county of Nantes, for 947-959 only; from 960 the Cliopatria shape without Nantes holds until 989

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 947-989 shape stops at lat 47.40 and leaves out Nantes (the 990 shape adds it). The County of Nantes page lists Alan II (938-952) and Drogo (952-960) as counts of Nantes as well as dukes, so Nantes belongs to the duchy until 960 (ledger loss 960, confidence 1). From 960 to 989 the shape stands as drawn: the page lists Hoel I (960-981) and Guerech (981-c.988) as counts of Nantes and Conan I as taking it 'by conquest' in 990. Area: the duchy page gives no figure.

37,206 km2 for 990-1146, with Nantes and the Retz country added in 990 (ledger gain 990: 'Conan I... Count of Nantes by conquest', 990-992). The duchy page has no area. The page says the dukes lost the Cotentin, Avranchin and Mayenne after 939, which the shape already omits.
37,363 km2: the same duchy, 1147-1151; the shape differs from 990 by one cell. Nothing on the page moves the border in these years.

correction.text: The 1152 shape without Nantes and its surrounding territories, from Michaelmas 1158; 1152-1157 stand as drawn

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria keeps Nantes in the duchy to 1187. The Conan IV page: 'At Michaelmas 1158, Conan IV surrendered Nantes and its surrounding territories to King Henry II at Avranches', and Henry held Nantes until 1185/1186; the County of Nantes page gives the county to Henry II 1158-1185. So Nantes leaves the shape from 1158 (1152-1157 stand). Under Angevin guardianship from 1166 (ledger occupation).

correction.text: The 1169 shape without Nantes and its surrounding territories, for 1169-1184; the full shape from 1185

keyframe_review.note: As for 1152: Nantes is Henry II's from 1158 until 1185/1186 ('Richmond and Nantes were held by Henry himself until 1183, and 1185/1186, respectively'). The County of Nantes page: 'Geoffrey II... holds the county' 1185-1186 and Constance 1185-1201, after which the county was 'merged permanently into the Ducal crown of Brittany'. The shape without Nantes holds for 1169-1184; Nantes returns in 1185 (ledger gain 1185).

correction.text: Brittany under Constance, Arthur I and Alix: 'John remained suzerain over Brittany, he was also vassal to Philip II of France' (Arthur I page)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for a Cliopatria gap: no Duchy row exists for 1188-1205 (the Angevin Empire row covers 1147-1209 and only touches Brittany), but the page has the duchy continuing: Constance duchess, 'Arthur I: Included in government in 1196', Arthur vanished in April 1203, then Alix with Guy of Thouars. The Arthur I page: 'In 1196, Constance had Arthur proclaimed Duke of Brittany and her co-ruler'. Shape = the 1187 shape.
37,320 km2, identical to the 1169 shape: Alix, then (from 1213) Peter of Dreux hold the whole duchy. The duchy page has no area figure.
37,387 km2 (one-cell change from 1206). Nothing on the page moves the border.
37,409 km2 (the largest Cliopatria Brittany shape). No dated territorial change on the page.
37,363 km2 (one-cell change). No dated territorial change on the page between 1294 and 1332 (John II d. 1305, Arthur II convokes the first Estates in 1309).

37,387 km2 for 1333-1343: the whole duchy until John III's death on 30 April 1341, and 'Mid-August 1341: John of Montfort held most of the duchy, including Nantes, Rennes, and Vannes'. The shape ignores the 1341-1343 civil war, handled as a contest (ledger 1341).

correction.text: the whole duchy of the 1333 shape; the English garrison at Brest is an occupation (ledger 1343-1397), not a loss of western Brittany

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria cuts the west (lon -4.91 to -4.10, about 7,100 km2) from 1344 to 1401 (30,270 km2). No page opened loses western Brittany to another state: the War of the Breton Succession page has an English garrison at Brest from 1343 ('1347: The English now controlled Brest, Quimper, and Vannes') and the First Treaty of Guérande (12 April 1365) 'established John of Montfort as Duke of Brittany' over the whole duchy. The whole duchy stays in the shape, with Brest hatched as English-occupied 1343-1397 (ledger occupation). The page does not say which side held Léon or Finistère in 1344.

correction.text: the whole duchy (the 1402 shape); Brest under English control until 1397

keyframe_review.note: As for 1344: the shape (30,246 km2) still lacks the west, but the John IV page has John 'sole master of the duchy' after the 12 April 1365 treaty, and 'In 1397, Duke John IV finally managed to extricate Brest from English control'. The French takeover attempt of 1378-1379 (du Guesclin, 'The Breton barons revolted against the takeover and invited Duke John IV back from exile in 1379') is a contest, not a loss. Whole duchy with Brest English-held to 1397.

37,363 km2: the whole duchy under John V (duke from 1399, d. 29 August 1442), restoring the west that Cliopatria drops 1344-1401; John IV had recovered Brest in 1397, five years before the shape returns.
37,206 km2 for 1422-1428: John V, who 'signed the Treaty of Troyes' and was held by the Penthièvre in 1420, rules the whole duchy; the page names no territorial change.

correction.text: the whole duchy under John V's neutrality, 1429-1439

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for a Cliopatria gap: no Duchy row for 1429-1439 although the page has John V ruling to 1442, 'to strengthen his duchy and to maintain its independence', 'remained formally aligned to the English cause, though in effect adopting a policy of careful neutrality'. Shape = the 1428 shape.
37,363 km2 for 1440-1452: John V (d. 1442) and Francis I, who 'pay[s] homage to Charles VII on 16 March 1446'; no territorial change on the page.
37,364 km2 for 1453-1481; the page names no change.
37,387 km2 for 1482-1486, the whole duchy before the Mad War reached it (French army enters in April 1487).

Cliopatria draws the whole duchy to 1491 although French troops held Châteaubriant, Vitré, Ancenis and Clisson from April 1487 and took Fougères and Dinan in July 1488; the pledged towns are handled as contest (1487-1488) and occupation (1488-1491) in the ledger.

correction.text: the whole duchy as a separate state in personal union under the queen-consort and then Claude and Francis III, to the 1532 union

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Duchy row after 1491, but the duchy outlived Anne's marriage: 'Upon his death in 1488, Anne became duchess', she 'made preserving the Duchy outside the French crown her life's work, although that goal would prove to have failed shortly after her death'; Claude was 'confirmed... Duchess' in 1514 and the Duchy page has the Estates proclaiming the union in 1532 (infobox 13 August 1547). Shape = the 1491 shape, in personal union with the French crown.

region.text: Brittany reconquered from the Norse, with the county of Nantes

ledger.note: 939: Alan II, Barbetorte, wins at Trans-la-Forêt and founds the duchy. 'On 1 August 939, with Judicael Berengar and Hugh I of Maine, Alan defeated the Vikings at Trans-la-Forêt'; infobox 'Independent duchy (939-942)'; the page also dates his return from England to both 936 and 937. In 942 'Alan paid homage to Louis IV of France for Brittany' (the vassal relation belongs to the West Franks dossier). The County of Nantes page lists Alan as Count of Nantes from 938, so Nantes is in the core.

region.text: the county of Nantes under Hoel I and Guerech

ledger.note: 960: Nantes leaves the ducal line (bridging a silence). The County of Nantes page lists Drogo as count 952-960, then Hoel I 960-981 and Guerech 981-c.988 as counts; the duchy page does not say when Nantes ceased to be part of the Rennes-based duchy. Cliopatria's 947-989 shape has no Nantes.

region.text: the county of Nantes, taken by conquest

ledger.note: 990: Conan I takes Nantes and styles himself duke. The County of Nantes page lists '990-992: Conan I, Count of Nantes by conquest'; the duchy page: 'Conan I: Became duke in 990. Died fighting Fulk III at Conquereuil on 27 June 992.' The extent (Nantes and the Retz country) is read from Cliopatria's 990 shape, which adds the south.
990: the House of Rennes takes the duchy with Conan I ('House of Rennes, Conan I: Became duke in 990'); the state, its colour and its land continue.

1066: the House of Cornouaille takes the duchy. 'Hawise (duchess) and Hoël II, House of Kernev/Cornouaille: Succeeded in 1066' after Conan II died; 'Hoël's line ruled until 1156'. Same state, same colour.

1158: Conan IV gives Nantes to Henry II. 'At Michaelmas 1158, Conan IV surrendered Nantes and its surrounding territories to King Henry II at Avranches.' The County of Nantes page agrees: 'the Breton duke awarded the county to Henry II' (1158-1185).

1164: Henry II seizes lands on the Normandy border. 'Henry seized lands along the Brittany-Normandy border' in 1164; the page names no place, so the region (the Couesnon marches around Mont-Saint-Michel) is a reading.

region.text: the whole duchy under Henry II's guardianship

ledger.note: 1166: Henry II invades and takes the duchy under his guardianship. 'Henry then forced Conan to abdicate as duke and to give Brittany to his heir and daughter Constance', Henry holding 'guardianship over Brittany for Constance until Geoffrey could marry her'; the duchy page: 'Henry II controlled the duchy from 1166'. Drawn as Angevin occupation of a duchy that keeps its own line (Constance); the page says Henry 'never formally became Duke'.

region.text: the whole duchy returns to its duchess and her husband Geoffrey

ledger.note: 1181: Geoffrey marries Constance and the duchy passes to them. The Conan IV page ties the end of Henry's own tenure of the duchy, Richmond (1183) and Nantes (1185/1186) to 'a marriage in 1181'; the duchy page has Constance and Geoffrey ruling jointly until 1186. The sentence is ambiguous about the duchy itself.

1185: Nantes returns to the duchy. The County of Nantes page: '1185-1186: Geoffrey II, Henry's fourth son, holds the county' and 'Constance... holds the county' 1185-1201; it was 'merged permanently into the Ducal crown of Brittany'. The Conan IV page says Henry held Nantes 'until... 1185/1186'.

1213: the House of Dreux takes the duchy. 'Alix's marriage to Peter in 1213 began the House of Dreux' (Peter Mauclerc); Philip II had arranged the marriage ('Philip replaced Guy as Alix's regent and then arranged her marriage to Pierre Mauclerc', Arthur I page). Same state, same colour.

region.text: the whole duchy: Nantes, Rennes, Vannes, Brest, Quimper, Auray

ledger.note: 1341: the Breton war of succession begins. 'On 30 April 1341, John III died'; 'Mid-August 1341: John of Montfort held most of the duchy, including Nantes, Rennes, and Vannes', then Charles of Blois' campaign: 'John was forced to surrender at Nantes' in the autumn. The whole duchy is the zone, Montfort (England) against Châtillon-Blois (France).

region.text: Brest and its hinterland, held by an English garrison

ledger.note: 1343: an English garrison holds Brest. 'A large permanent English garrison was held at Brest'; Joan of Flanders had been driven into Brest in 1342 and the English relieved the siege on 18 August 1342; 'Montfort-held places were administered from London'; by 1347 'the English now controlled Brest, Quimper, and Vannes'. Brest stays English until 1397 (John IV page).

1365: the war ends at Guérande. 'Peace was concluded on 12 April 1365 by the First Treaty of Guérande', which 'established John of Montfort as Duke of Brittany'; Charles of Blois had been killed at Auray on 29 September 1364.

1365: the House of Montfort takes the duchy. John of Montfort (John IV; the John IV page: 'Duke of Brittany... from 1345') is established as duke by the 12 April 1365 treaty and in December 1366 swears an oath to Charles V of France; the Blois-Penthièvre claim ends. Same state, same colour.

1378: Charles V tries to annex the duchy. 'King Charles V made the mistake of attempting to completely adjoin the duchy of Brittany to France'; 'Bertrand de Guesclin was sent to make the duchy submit to the French king by force of arms in 1378'. John IV had gone into exile in England in 1373.
1379: the Breton barons recall John IV. 'The Breton barons revolted against the takeover and invited Duke John IV back from exile in 1379'; he landed at Dinard; he later reconciled with Charles VI.
1397: Brest is recovered from the English. 'In 1397, Duke John IV finally managed to extricate Brest from English control.' Cliopatria restores the west only in 1402.

region.text: eastern Brittany: Châteaubriant, Vitré, Ancenis, Clisson, Fougères and Dinan

ledger.note: 1487: the French army enters Brittany. In April 1487 the royal army 'was accommodated favorably in Châteaubriant, Vitré, Ancenis, and Clisson'; it besieged Nantes, but 'Cornish allies of Brittany, helped by foreign mercenaries, broke the siege'. The page dates the Mad War 1485-1488; the royal-allied Viscount de Rohan 'held the north of the duchy, and took Ploërmel'.

region.text: eastern Brittany: the territories conquered by France

ledger.note: 1488: Saint-Aubin-du-Cormier ends the war. 'The Breton forces, led by Marshal de Rieux, were decisively beaten by the French' on 28 July 1488 (royal forces had taken Fougères on 12 July, then Dinan); the Treaty of Sablé of 20 August 1488 has Francis II acknowledge himself the king's vassal and 'pledge the territories conquered by France'.

region.text: the pledged towns under French garrisons: Fougères, Saint-Aubin-du-Cormier and Dinan

ledger.note: 1488: French garrisons hold the pledged towns. After Sablé Charles VIII withdrew his forces from Brittany 'except for the town garrisons of the territories pledged by Francis'; the page does not name the towns, so the region is the zone the war took (Fougères, Dinan, Saint-Aubin-du-Cormier and the Châteaubriant-Clisson march). Reviewer eu-10-a narrowed the region from the whole of Ille-et-Vilaine and Loire-Atlantique to the towns the page has the French take ('On 12 July, royal forces captured Fougères and then Dinan'): Rennes, where Anne was crowned on 10 February 1489, and Nantes were not French-garrisoned in 1488-1491.

region.text: the pledged towns (Fougères, Saint-Aubin-du-Cormier, Dinan), absorbed in the union under the crown

ledger.note: 1491: Rennes falls and Anne marries Charles VIII. 'Rennes lasted through two months of Charles's siege before falling'; 'Charles VIII entered the city on 15 November'; the marriage 'was celebrated in the Great Hall of the Château de Langeais on 6 December 1491'. The contract let the survivor keep Brittany; the duchy stays a separate state in personal union with the crown until 1532, so the garrisons end here without annexation. Cliopatria ends the duchy this year.

region.text: the whole duchy, united with the French crown

ledger.note: 1532: the Estates of Brittany proclaim the union with France. 'The Estates proclaimed union in 1532'; the infobox dates the union to 13 August 1547 ('Union with France'). Anne, Claude (duchess 1514-1524) and Francis III (d. 1536) had held the duchy in the meantime. The land passes to the Kingdom of France.

wars.name: War of the Breton Succession

zones.text: the whole duchy: Nantes, Rennes, Vannes, Brest, Quimper, Auray

wars.outcome: Montfort victory: Charles of Blois killed at Auray on 29 September 1364; the First Treaty of Guérande of 12 April 1365 established John of Montfort as duke, with Joan of Penthièvre giving up her rights.
wars.note: Infobox 1341 - 12 April 1365. The English hold Brest from 1343 (ledger 1343-1397).

wars.name: Mad War

zones.text: eastern Brittany: Châteaubriant, Vitré, Ancenis, Clisson, Fougères, Dinan, Saint-Aubin-du-Cormier

wars.outcome: French victory at Saint-Aubin-du-Cormier (28 July 1488); the Treaty of Sablé (20 August 1488) makes Francis II the king's vassal and pledges the conquered territories to France; Rennes falls in 1491 and Anne marries Charles VIII.
wars.note: The page gives the war as 1485-1488, with a second phase from June 1486 to November 1488.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey draws the duchy's frontier in any page opened; the marches with Normandy, Maine and Anjou are feudal and approximate. The 1365 Guérande treaty and the 1488 Sablé treaty settle who rules, not a boundary.

notes: Pages: 9 of 9 budgeted. Cliopatria rows: the Duchy row has gaps (1188-1205, 1429-1439, and nothing after 1491) that are not gaps in the pages; new keyframes _1188, _1429, _1492 fill them. 1344-1401 (30.3k km2) drops the west (lon -4.91 to -4.10) and no page opened explains it; adjusted to the whole duchy with Brest English-occupied 1343-1397. 947-989 omits Nantes (adjusted for 947-959). Ends: Cliopatria stops the duchy at 1491 (Anne's marriage), the Duchy page keeps it separate: 'The Estates proclaimed union in 1532', infobox 13 August 1547. The dossier ends in 1532 and the 1492-1532 keyframe is the 1491 shape; the Kingdom of France dossier (eu-10) should show Brittany as a personal-union/vassal tint in that span and not as direct domain, or the orchestrator may cut the end back to 1491. Counterparts needing dossiers: county-of-nantes (Hoel I, Guerech and the counts of Nantes, 960-990; the page lists them), House of Châtillon-Blois / Penthièvre (a party, not a state). The homage to Louis IV in 942 and to Charles VII in 1446 (Francis I, 16 March 1446) are vassal relations that belong in the west-franks and kingdom-of-france ledgers. Not done: rulers (the duchy page gives a partial dukes list without reign years for several entries); capitals by year (the infobox lists Nantes, Rennes and Vannes without years); the English Brest garrison before 1343 (the page has the siege relieved on 18 August 1342) and the Cotentin, Avranchin and Mayenne losses after 939 (page gives no year; the Kingdom of Brittany dossier carries 933). No page opened gives a Brittany area, so the keyframe areas could not be compared with an infobox. Gazetteer: 'Brest' resolves to the French city only when country is given.
